newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia landlord charged with murder after fire.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia landlord charged with murder after fire.

text.p: Prosecutors Thursday asked the landlord of a West Philadelphia apartment building to surrender after charging him with murder in connection with a fatal fire last month.
John Gray, of Lawnside, N.J., faces six counts of murder, involuntary manslaughter and other charges arising from the April 5 blaze in a converted townhouse, said District Attorney Lynn Abraham.
The suspected cause of the fire was a faulty electrical outlet.
Killed in the fire were a couple and four of the woman's five children. Another child survived. Ten firefighters were injured.
Gray, 64, was interviewed at the time of the fire and released. Abraham, who appealed to Gray to surrender, said her office had been in touch with his attorney.
The building was cited for fire code violations Oct. 27, 1996, and again on Nov. 7 by a city buildings inspector, Abraham told reporters.
